greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Here's your Friday round-up, with a big day in tech and a Victorian election on the horizon.

lead.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns with immediate effect
lead.summary: Nvidia told the SEC on 12 November that Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO, president and board member. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, and Harvey C. Jones becomes the company's first board chair.

stories.headline: An AI-native lab runs biomolecular experiments autonomously
stories.summary: Published in Nature on 4 November, this Shanghai Jiao Tong University work describes AutoDNA, a system where AI agents plan experiments, write control code and drive more than 20 lab instruments. It is drawing attention for running thousands of steps over about eight days, though people still had to restock reagents and fix some hardware faults.

stories.headline: Hidden fractal limit found on how predictable deep-learning training can be
stories.summary: Sydney researchers report in Nature Machine Intelligence that training outcomes sit in fractal 'riddled' basins, so even vastly more precise starting settings did not make results more reproducible. The paper is getting coverage for what it implies about AI reproducibility.

stories.headline: Transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo for excited molecular states (preprint)
stories.summary: Noé's group describes a neural-network wavefunction method that shares weights across geometries to map excited-state energy surfaces far more cheaply. Note this link is the arXiv preprint; a Nature Computational Science version was reported in early November but I could not open it.

stories.headline: Anthropic files public S-1 for its IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic has publicly filed its registration statement with the SEC, with figures such as more than 11,900 customers paying over $100,000 a year. Reports describe it as a controlled company under Nasdaq rules.

stories.headline: Huang's exit rocks the company at the centre of the AI boom
stories.summary: Fortune's earlier coverage describes a board investigation into Huang's conduct, which preceded his resignation. It frames how much of Nvidia's power was built around him.

stories.headline: Daily AI roundup: funding, security and model news
stories.summary: A digest of Friday's AI developments, including Anthropic's training-academy commitment and a robotics funding round. Details come from a newsletter, so check the original reports.

stories.headline: Victorian election live: UN adviser criticises plan to scrap Treaty
stories.summary: With Victorians voting on 28 November, ABC's live blog covers the campaign, including criticism from a UN adviser of the opposition's plan to scrap the state's Treaty.

stories.headline: Gippsland local news briefing, Friday 13 November
stories.summary: ABC's regional briefing rounds up the day's Gippsland stories, including a camping teenager reported found after days missing near Walhalla East.

stories.headline: Central Victoria local news briefing, Friday 13 November
stories.summary: The regional briefing summarises the latest local news across central Victoria for the day.

stories.headline: Euronews morning bulletin, 13 November
stories.summary: Euronews' bulletin rounds up the day's top international stories, with coverage of the Middle East, Ukraine and Asia.

stories.headline: Friday morning news: Iran tensions and Ukraine talks
stories.summary: WORLD's morning roundup reports US-Israel friction over Iran and ongoing discussion of the next round of Ukraine talks.

thought: The best way to predict the future is to invent it. — Alan Kay
